tool.name: detect CRISPR sequences
tool.command:
## minced reads the FASTA through a plain java.io.FileReader and has no gzip ## support, so gzipped inputs are unpacked into a job-local FASTA that every ## minced invocation below uses as its input. #if $input.is_of_type('fasta.gz'): gunzip -c '$input' > minced_input.fasta && #else: ln -s '$input' minced_input.fasta && #end if
## The spacers FASTA is written next to the report as <report>_spacers.fa, where ## minced strips everything after the first dot of the report name, so the report ## name must not contain a dot (a mktemp() path would therefore be wrong). temp_output='minced_report';
## All flags must precede the positional arguments. Since 0.4.2 a flag placed ## after the last positional is silently consumed as the GFF file name instead. ## The options are identical for every invocation, so collect them once. minced_opts="-minNR $minNR -minRL $minRL -maxRL $maxRL -minSL $minSL -maxSL $maxSL"; #if str($searchWL) != 'none': minced_opts="\$minced_opts -searchWL $searchWL"; #end if
## Pass 1: the plain text report. This is the only invocation that emits the ## "Sequence '<id>' (<n> bp)" header lines that reformat.py needs to name the ## BED / tabular rows, so it must never be combined with -gff / -gffFull. minced \$minced_opts #if '-spacers' in $outputs: -spacers #end if minced_input.fasta \$temp_output ;
#if 'BED' in $outputs or 'TABULAR' in $outputs: ## reformat.py is only needed to derive the BED / tabular outputs python $__tool_directory__/reformat.py \$temp_output results.bed results.tab; #end if
#if '-spacers' in $outputs: mv \$temp_output'_spacers.fa' $output_fasta; #end if
## Since 0.3.0 minced takes an optional third positional for the GFF file. When it is ## omitted the GFF *replaces* the text report and the report additionally loses its ## "Sequence '<id>'" header line, so the GFF passes are run separately and always ## write to an explicit GFF path, leaving the report from pass 1 intact. #if '-gffFull' in $outputs: gff_report_full=\$(mktemp); minced \$minced_opts -gffFull minced_input.fasta \$gff_report_full results_full.gff ; #end if #if '-gff' in $outputs: gff_report=\$(mktemp); minced \$minced_opts -gff minced_input.fasta \$gff_report results.gff ; #end if

param.name: minNR
param.label: Minimum number of repeats a CRISPER must have

param.name: minRL
param.label: Minimum length of a CRISPER repeated region

param.name: maxRL
param.label: Maximum length of a CRISPER repeated region

param.name: minSL
param.label: Minimum length of CRISPER non repeated region

param.name: maxSL
param.label: Maximum length of CRISPER non repeated region

param.name: searchWL
param.label: Length of search window to used to discover CRISPERs

param.name: outputs
param.label: Additional output format
param.option: fasta formatted file containing the spacers

tool.help:
MinCED - Mining CRISPRs in Environmental Datasets
MinCED is a program to find Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPRs) in full genomes or environmental datasets such as metagenomes, in which sequence size can be anywhere from 100 to 800 bp. MinCED was derived from CRT.
**Upstream documentation**
[https://github.com/ctSkennerton/minced](https://github.com/ctSkennerton/minced)
-----
# Outputs
Depending on the selection under *Additional output format* the tool produces:
- **BED** — one interval per detected CRISPR array, in zero-based, half-open coordinates as required by the BED format - **Tabular** — one row per repeat/spacer unit with the repeat position, the repeat and spacer sequences and their lengths - **GFF (summary / detailed)** — `repeat_region` features, or additionally the individual `repeat_unit` features when the detailed variant is selected - **Spacer sequences** — the extracted spacers as FASTA
-----
# Notes
- For raw short reads (100-200 bp) use [Crass](https://github.com/ctskennerton/Crass) instead. - Since minced 0.3.2 repeats that touch the edge of a contig are discarded, so a partial repeat or spacer at the very end of a sequence may be lost.
-----
If you use this tool in Galaxy, please cite Gruening, BA et al. [https://github.com/bgruening/galaxytools](https://github.com/bgruening/galaxytools)
